messages:
oliver: Heads-up — we started seeing a spike in schema validation rejects on tool invocations around 18:02 UTC. Lots of requests are being routed to hosted fallback which blew past quota alerts. Not a huge volume, but enough to trigger billing spikes and noisy dashboards.
maya: ugh. do we know if it's a new model rollout or recent change to the schema validator?
dom: looks like validator strictness was flipped to "true" in the canary config yesterday for a small rollout. change id: cfg/rl-622.
jen (sre): can you paste an example error? need to see if these are malformed responses vs validator bug.
oliver: here's a sanitized example from logs (raw toolcall payload + validator trace):
```json
{"request_id":"r-9a1b","route":"orders/charge","tool":"payment-service","response":{"status":"ok","body":{"amount":"9.99","currency":"usd"}},"validator_error":"type mismatch at body.amount: expected number got string"}
```
maya: oh, body.amount is string — old clients sent strings, new schema expects number. That'd trigger rejects. The funny bit is routing policy then tries hosted fallback rather than returning a structured schema error upstream.
dom: routing policy is: on model error -> try same-route fallback; on schema rejection -> reroute to hosted if dedicated fails. That was intended to keep live traffic, but it means hosted tokens get used on inconsistent responses.
lee (product): from a UX perspective, hosted fallback for schema issues is surprising. Product owners see errors in the console labelled as "hosted usage" rather than "schema rejects" and it's confusing for billing/ownership.
console-bot: new metric missing: schema_reject_rate by route. Proposed panel: "Schema rejects (rate) — per route, 5m/1h". There is currently only a counter for tool_failures which conflates network/model/schema.
jen (sre): action item: we need a stop-gap to avoid hosted quota burn. Suggest changing routing policy so schema rejections return a structured error to caller (HTTP 422) instead of doing hosted fallback. Then trigger an opt-in relaxed mode for customers with legacy clients.
dom: technically doable. We'll change routing to treat VALIDATION_FAILURE as terminal if the request came from dedicated/private. Add a routing flag: allow_schema_fallback=true by default for older tenants, but opt-out at tenant-level.
oliver: also telemetry: we don't have a clear tag on why fallback happened. Right now fallback_reason is just "model_error" or "resource". Need to add codes: VALIDATION_REJECT, SCHEMA_MISMATCH, TOOL_TIMEOUT. Otherwise console charts misattribute.
maya: +1. can we also add a sampling log that captures the failing payload example and schema version id? Helps debugging without logging full PII.
jen (sre): timeline? We should patch routing policy during maintenance window to avoid accidental regressions. Also add autopager to alerting so SRE gets paged if hosted quota usage > 10% delta due to fallbacks.
dom: I'll open RFC and a small PR: 1) routing change (make VALIDATION_FAILURE terminal), 2) add fallback_reason codes, 3) tenant flag allow_schema_fallback. Will target canary next Wed.
lee (product): for Console UX: add a dedicated dashboard tile for "Schema rejects" and break down by route/model/schema_version. Also add explanatory tooltip: "Schema rejects indicate the model output didn't match the expected structured contract — these are not runtime model errors."
console-bot: noted. Dashboard PR template: add panel, add alert rule (rate > 0.5% sustained), link to docs page.
deploy-bot: canary deploy scheduled for 2026-04-01 03:00 UTC (window: 2h).
oliver: one more ask — telemetry sampling for validation failures should include: route, schema_id, tenant_id, sample_response_snippet (first 256 chars), fallback_reason. No raw PII.
maya: also consider adding a v2 validator compatibility mode: if schema_v2 isn't compatible, validator can coerce obvious type mismatches ("9.99" -> 9.99) when allow_relaxed_validation flag is on. But this should be opt-in per tenant.
jen (sre): coercion is dangerous for fraud-sensitive routes (payments). For those routes, we should never coerce. Add per-route enforcement-level in the route config.
dom: agreed. Implementation plan in RFC will include route-level enforcement. I'll include a sample config snippet: 
```yaml
route: orders/charge
schema_enforcement: strict # options: strict, warn, relax
allow_schema_fallback: false
```
lee (product): i'll file a docs ticket to clarify what customers will see in Console and propose a short changelog email for impacted tenants.
oliver: ok team — next steps: dom to open RFC + PR, jen to update on-call alerting, console to add panel + alert, maya to coordinate docs. We'll reconvene after canary results. Thanks. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: canary completed: 10% traffic -> success. No regressions in canary segment.
jen (sre): after canary we'll run a simulated legacy-client test to ensure rejects behave as expected.
oliver: assigning follow-ups in issue tracker (INF-4829).
